ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r3.claim: The surah's historical examples show that God controls individuals and nations, gives respite as He wills, and seizes them when their term ends; none can exceed His limits.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r3.anchor: Similar is His dealing with nations.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r1.claim: The fates of powerful nations prove God's control: after respite, those who cross His limits are seized helplessly despite their power and glory.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r1.anchor: When they wrongly use their freedom to exercise their will and cross the limits set for them by the Almighty, they are given respite

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p307/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p307/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p307/r1.claim: God grants nations a wise respite to mend their ways, then seizes them; their destruction anticipates accountability for every person, with full reward or punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p307/r1.anchor: the whole world also will be held accountable one day in which each and every individual will be held responsible for his deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p308/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p308/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p308/r3.claim: The nations' rebellion meant indifference and fearlessness toward God, coupled with the conceit that their status and resources were self-earned and beyond accountability.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p308/r3.anchor: These people were rebellious in their lands

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p309/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p309/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p309/r2.claim: God's established practice is to monitor nations entrusted with political power, allow time for reform or a final communication of truth, and destroy persistently rebellious nations; even those at their zenith cannot avert it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p309/r2.anchor: He continues to watch over it and sees if it is properly using this authority.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r3.claim: Al-ladhina can modify ʿAd, Thamud, and Pharaoh, stand as an object of blame, or be nominative after an omitted pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r3.anchor: الذين صفة لعاد وثمود وفرعون، أو منصوب على الذم

TABRISI:89:1-30#7/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#7/r4.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:89:1-30#7/r4.claim: Aad, Thamud, and Pharaoh transgressed against God's prophets and spread killing and sin throughout the land.
TABRISI:89:1-30#7/r4.anchor: يعني عادا وثمود وفرعون طغوا أي تجبروا في البلاد على أنبياء الله

BURSEVI:v10p330/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p330/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p330/r1.claim: He prefers construing 'those who transgressed' as a genitive adjective of the three groups because this needs no ellipsis, while al-Zamakhshari prefers accusative as a reproach with implied 'I mean,' which better suits the meaning.
BURSEVI:v10p330/r1.anchor: وهو أحسن بحسب اللفظ إذ لا حذف فيه واختار صاحب الكشاف كونه منصوبا على الذم

BURSEVI:v10p330/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p330/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p330/r2.claim: Each group transgressed in its own territory: Aad in Yemen, Thamud in Syria, Egyptians in Egypt, and Nimrod in Sawad.
BURSEVI:v10p330/r2.anchor: طغى عاد في اليمن وثمود بأرض الشأم والقبط بمصر

IBNASHUR:89:11/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:11/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:11/r1.claim: The phrase about those who transgress may describe all three peoples or specifically Pharaoh and his people.
IBNASHUR:89:11/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون شاملاً لجميع المذكورين عاد وثمود وفرعون . ويجوز أن يكون نعتاً لفرعون

IBNASHUR:89:11/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:11/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:11/r2.claim: Ṭughyān means extreme disobedience and injustice; each people transgressed in its own land, and local oppression spreads through the lands.
IBNASHUR:89:11/r2.anchor: والطغيان شدّة العصيان والظلم ومعنى طغيانهم في البلاد أن كل أمة من هؤلاء طغوا في بلدهم

IBNASHUR:89:11/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:11/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:11/r3.claim: Tyranny multiplies corruption by teaching others to violate rights; it also breeds hatred and fear, divides society, and weakens its ability to face external enemies.
IBNASHUR:89:11/r3.anchor: فلا جرم كان الطغيان سبباً لكثرة الفساد

IBNASHUR:89:11/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:11/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:11/r4.claim: Al-bilād may use a familiar referent for the lands of those peoples, with the plural distributed so each nation is assigned its own land.
IBNASHUR:89:11/r4.anchor: أي في بلادهم والجمع على اعتبار التوزيع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p317/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p317/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p317/r1.claim: The historical lessons either constitute evidence for an omitted oath-answer, or precede “Your Lord is indeed watching” to build suspense and prepare the audience for that answer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p317/r1.anchor: فهذه العبر جزئيات من مضمون جواب القسم ، فإن كان محذوفا فذكرها دليله ، وإن كان الجواب قوله : { إن ربك لبالمرصاد }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p321/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p321/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p321/r1.claim: The clause about those who transgressed may describe all three named peoples, or specifically Pharaoh and his people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p321/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون شاملا لجميع المذكورين عاد وثمود وفرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p321/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p321/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p321/r2.claim: Tughyān is extreme disobedience and injustice; each nation transgressed in its own land, with the plural distributive or contextually restricted to their lands.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p321/r2.anchor: والطغيان شدة العصيان والظلم ومعنى طغيانهم في البلاد أن كل أمة من هؤلاء طغوا في بلدهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p321/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p321/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p321/r4.claim: The definite article in al-bilād may refer to the lands already mentioned; the plural distributes the action so each nation transgressed in its own country.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p321/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التعريف في { البلاد } تعريف العهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p117#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p117#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p117#3/r1.claim: The transgressors are ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh; they committed sins and tyrannized God's prophets.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p117#3/r1.anchor: الذين طغوا في البلاد يعني عادا وثمود وفوعون عملوا بالمعاصي وتجبروا على أنبياء الله

JISHUMI:v10p7403/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r2.claim: Ṭughyān means exceeding the limit in corruption, like water going beyond its boundary.
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r2.anchor: والطغيان: مجاوزة الحد في الإفساد، ومنه: (طغى الماء)

KASHSHAF:89:11/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:11/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:11/r1.claim: The best syntax places those who transgressed in the accusative as a censure; nominative as a new clause or genitive as an adjective are also possible.
KASHSHAF:89:11/r1.anchor: أحسن الوجوه فيه أن يكون في محل النصب على الذم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p750#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p750#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p750#2/r10.claim: Alladhina taghaw is best parsed as an accusative of blame; it can also be nominative or genitive as a modifier of Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p750#2/r10.anchor: أو مجرورا على وصف المذكورين عاد وثمود وفرعون

MUQATIL:89:11-14/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:89:11-14/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:89:11-14/r1.claim: The transgressors, continuing the reference to ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh, committed sins in the lands.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#4/r1.claim: The relative pronoun can be accusative as censure, nominative as an implied “they are,” or genitive as a description of Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh; they transgressed in the lands.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#4/r1.anchor: فى محل النصب على الذم أو الرفع على هم الذين أو الجر على وصف المذكورين عاد وثمود وفرعون

QURTUBI-FULL:89:11-13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:11-13/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:11-13/r2.claim: He prefers construing ‘those who transgressed’ as an accusative phrase of censure; it can also be nominative (‘they are’) or genitive as an adjective for the named peoples.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:11-13/r2.anchor: أحسن الوجوه فيه أن يكون في محل النصب على الذم

NAHHAS:v5p221/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p221/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p221/r8.claim: They transgressed God's command in the lands and lived there.
NAHHAS:v5p221/r8.anchor: أي تجاوزوا أمر الله جل وعز في البلاد أي الذين كانوا فيه

QUTB-ZILAL:89:11/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:11/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:11/r1.claim: Tyranny corrupts the tyrant, the oppressed, social bonds, and the sound order of life; the tyrant becomes enslaved to desire and claims God's place, as Pharaoh did.
QUTB-ZILAL:89:11/r1.anchor: لأنه لا يفيء إلى ميزان ثابت

QUTB-ZILAL:89:11/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:11/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:11/r2.claim: Tyranny humiliates the masses, suppressing dignity and creativity and cultivating resentment, degraded desires, and lost ambition.

QUTB-ZILAL:89:11/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:11/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:11/r3.claim: Tyrants falsify values and standards because upright measures threaten their power, making oppression seem acceptable.

RAZI:89:11/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:11/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:89:11/r1.claim: The pronoun in “those who transgressed” may refer only to Pharaoh, its nearest antecedent, but al-Razi prefers that it include everyone previously mentioned.
RAZI:89:11/r1.anchor: يرجع إلى جميع من تقدم ذكرهم ، وهذا هو الأقرب

RAZI:89:11/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:11/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:89:11/r2.claim: The best parsing puts “those who transgressed” in the accusative as censure; nominative predication or genitive description of ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh are also possible.
RAZI:89:11/r2.anchor: أحسن الوجوه في إعرابه أن يكون في محل النصب على الذم

RAZI:89:11/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:11/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:89:11/r3.claim: Their transgression means committing sins and tyrannizing over God’s prophets and believers.
RAZI:89:11/r3.anchor: عملوا المعاصي وتجبروا على أنبياء الله والمؤمنين

SAMIN-DURR:89:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:11/r1.claim: Alladhīna may modify the preceding phrase or be detached as a censure; sawṭ is the familiar whip, perhaps named because it mixes flesh when striking.
SAMIN-DURR:89:11/r1.anchor: قوله: { الذين طغوا }: يجوز فيه ما جاز في " الذين " قبله

STUDYQURAN:89:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:11/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:11/r1.claim: The tyranny and corruption described apply to all three peoples named in verses 6–10.
STUDYQURAN:89:11/r1.anchor: These verses refer to all three groups mentioned in vv. 6–10

TAB:89:11/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:11/r1.speaker: author
TAB:89:11/r1.claim: The people who transgressed in the lands are ʿĀd, Thamūd, Pharaoh, and his troops; they exceeded what God permitted and defiantly committed prohibited disbelief in their lands.
TAB:89:11/r1.anchor: يعني بقوله جلّ ثناؤه الذين عادا وثمود وفرعون وجنده .   ويعني بقوله :  طَغَوْا :  تجاوزوا ما أباحه لهم ربهم

TABATABAI:89:9-15/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:9-15/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:9-15/r6.claim: The description applies jointly to ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh: they transgressed in the lands and spread corruption.
TABATABAI:89:9-15/r6.anchor: صفة للمذكورين من عاد وثمود وفرعون

TABRISI:89:25/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:25/r8.speaker: القواس، البزي، يعقوب
TABRISI:89:25/r8.claim: Al-Qawwās, al-Bazzī, and Yaʿqūb retain the yāʾ in bi-l-wādī both when joining and pausing.
TABRISI:89:25/r8.anchor: وقرأ القواس والبزي ويعقوب بالوادي بإثبات الياء في الوصل والوقف

TABRISI:89:25/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:25/r9.speaker: ورش
TABRISI:89:25/r9.claim: Warsh retains that yāʾ in connected reading but drops it at pause; the other readers omit it in both contexts.
TABRISI:89:25/r9.anchor: وورش بإثباتها في الوصل وحذفها في الوقف

THALABI:v10p199/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p199/r3.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p199/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses the scourge as a kind of punishment poured on the transgressors.
THALABI:v10p199/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: يعني لونا من العذاب صبه عليهم

ELMALILI:89:10-15/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r10.claim: Proud of their strength and ruled by desire, these peoples exceeded the bounds of justice and violated the rights of people and their Creator.
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r10.anchor: hak ve adalet hudûdunu aşıp halkın ve Hâlık’ın hukūkuna tasallut ve tecavüzde ileri gitmişlerdi

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r4.claim: An early Zuhair verse lists Pharaoh among figures God destroyed, resembling Quranic punishment catalogues of historical actors, though Zuhair lists individuals rather than collectives; Quranic cycles may develop related ideas.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Offensichtlich hat man es hier mit einer koranischen Straflisten durchaus vergleichbaren Zusammenstellung geschichtlicher Akteure zu tun (bei Zuhair sind es allerdings Individuen und keine Kollektive)

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:11:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:11:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:11:anmerkung/r1.claim: For the root ṭ-ġ-w/y, the note refers to 96:6.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:11:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zur Wurzel ṭ-ġ-w/y s. die Anmerkung zu 96:6.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r1.claim: The destroyed peoples show later generations that material strength cannot avert divine punishment for denial and rebellion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r1.anchor: geçmişte bazı toplulukların inkâr ve azgınlıkları yüzünden nasıl helâk edildiklerine, maddî güç ve imkânları olsa da bunların kendilerini ilâhî cezadan kurtaramadığına dikkat çekilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r7.claim: The first audience likely knew these peoples’ stories by hearsay or had seen or heard of their ruins; their recurring traits were great strength and unrestrained corruption and rebellion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r7.anchor: Bu âyetlerde söz konusu edilen kavimlerin iki özelliğine dikkat çekildiği görülmektedir: İlki çok güçlü olmaları, ikincisi de ülkelerinde azgınlığa sapmaları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r8.claim: The warning applies to rulers and other responsible people: those who disregard God’s guidance and justice and turn a country into an arena of sedition and corruption deserve inevitable disaster.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r8.anchor: hak ve adalet ölçülerinden sapar ve sonuçta ülkeyi fitne fesat ortamı haline getirirlerse, kaçınılmaz felâketi de hak etmiş olurlar

ALUSI-FULL:v30p124#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124#3/r1.claim: The clause may be a genitive adjective for the named peoples, or nominative or accusative as a clause of censure; on the latter parsing each tyrant is meant.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124#3/r1.anchor: الذين طغوا في البلاد إما مجرور على أنه صفة للمذكورين عاد ومن بعده أو منصوب أو مرفوع على الذم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p420#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p420#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p420#2/r1.claim: The transgressors were Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh, who disobeyed and behaved arrogantly in the land.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p420#2/r1.anchor: يعني عادا وثمود وفرعون، عملوا في الأرض بالمعاصي وتجبروا

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:10-14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:10-14/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:10-14/r2.claim: Those who transgressed can syntactically qualify ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh, or can be a separate expression of blame in either case ending.

BINTSHATI:v2p138/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p138/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p138/r6.claim: The Qur'an cites ʿĀd, Iram, Thamūd, and Pharaoh for the moral lesson, whereas exegetes have filled in details on which they disagree widely.
BINTSHATI:v2p138/r6.anchor: وقد أكثر المفسرون في الكلام عن عاد إرم ذات العماد، وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد، وفرعون ذي الأوتاد

BINTSHATI:v2p146/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p146/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p146/r4.claim: The surah directs readers to the core lesson: tyrants exceeded bounds, spread corruption, and were met with punishment under God's watch; further catalogues of their sins are unnecessary.
BINTSHATI:v2p146/r4.anchor: ويتجه البيان القرآني، بما لفت إليه مما فعل ربك بعاد وثمود وفرعوم، إلى مناط العبرة وجوهر الموقف

BINTSHATI:v2p147/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p147/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p147/r1.claim: Ṭughyān means exceeding bounds, first used of water overflowing into a flood, then of the overreaching arrogance of tyrants; the author had discussed it in Moses' charge to Pharaoh.
BINTSHATI:v2p147/r1.anchor: والطغيان تجاوز الحد، وأصل استعماله في الماء يطغى فيغرق

BINTSHATI:v2p147/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p147/r2.speaker: المفسرون واللغويون
BINTSHATI:v2p147/r2.claim: Exegetes and grammarians parse alladhīna ṭaghaw three ways: accusative for blame, nominative after an implied subject, or genitive as an adjective.
BINTSHATI:v2p147/r2.anchor: وللغويين والمفسرين في إعراب جملة {الَّذِينَ طَغَوْا} ثلاثة أوجه:

BINTSHATI:v2p147/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p147/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p147/r3.claim: All three parses are formally valid but not rhetorically equal; the author prefers linking the clause as a modifier to what precedes, rather than as blame or a separate sentence with an implied subject.
BINTSHATI:v2p147/r3.anchor: ونرى ربطه بالصلة على وجه الإتباع لما قبله، أولى من الاختصاص

BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r5.claim: The plural description collectively covers Pharaoh, his army, Ad, Thamud, and their followers: they exceeded bounds in lands they ruled and spread unbelief and injustice as an imitated precedent.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r5.anchor: فرعون وجنوده وكل من ذكر هنا من الكفرة من عاد وثمود وأتباعهم

ABUHAYYAN:89:11/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:11/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:11/r1.claim: Alladhīna can modify ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh, or be accusative for censure, or nominative with an omitted subject.
ABUHAYYAN:89:11/r1.anchor: { الذين } صفة لعاد وثمود وفرعون ، أو منصوب على الذم ، أو مرفوع على إضمارهم

ALUSI:89:11/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:11/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:11/r1.claim: The phrase may be genitive as an adjective for the groups named, or nominative or accusative for censure, meaning each tyrant transgressed in his own land; the same parsing applies to 89:12.
ALUSI:89:11/r1.anchor: إما مجرور على أنه صفة للمذكورين عاد ومن بعده أو منصوب أو مرفوع على الذم

BAGHAWI:89:11/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:11/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:89:11/r1.claim: The transgressors are ʿAd, Thamud, and Pharaoh; they sinned and acted arrogantly on earth.
BAGHAWI:89:11/r1.anchor: يعني عاداً وثمود وفرعون ،   عملوا في الأرض بالمعاصي وتجبروا

BAYDAWI:89:11/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:11/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:11/r1.claim: The clause describes the previously mentioned ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh, or it can stand as an accusative or nominative expression of blame.
BAYDAWI:89:11/r1.anchor: الذين طغوا في البلاد صفة للمذكورين عاد وثمود وفرعون أو ذم منصوب أو مرفوع

BIQAI:89:11/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:11/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:11/r1.claim: Pharaoh's name stands for him and his troops: the head represents the body because the group is collective and depends on its leader.
BIQAI:89:11/r1.anchor: لأن الرأس يكنى به عن البدن ، لأنه جماعة وبه قوامه

BIQAI:89:11/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:11/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:11/r2.claim: The plural relative refers to Pharaoh and his troops, and to all the disbelievers already named, including ʿĀd, Thamūd, and their followers.
BIQAI:89:11/r2.anchor: أي فرعون وجنوده وكل من ذكر هنا من الكفرة من عاد وثمود وأتباعهم

BIQAI:89:11/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:11/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:11/r3.claim: Ṭaghaw means they transgressed the bounds.

BIQAI:89:11/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:11/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:11/r4.claim: Their transgression covered the lands they actually ruled and those they could dominate by force.
BIQAI:89:11/r4.anchor: أي التي ملكوها بالفعل وغيرها بالقوة

IBNKATHIR:89:11/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:11/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:11/r1.claim: They rebelled and acted insolently in the lands, spreading corruption and harming people.
IBNKATHIR:89:11/r1.anchor: أي : تمردوا وعتوا وعاثوا في الأرض بالإفساد والأذية للناس

NASAFI:89:11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:11/r1.claim: Alladhina can be accusative as a denunciation, nominative with an implied ‘they are,’ or genitive as an adjective for the previously mentioned ‘Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh.
NASAFI:89:11/r1.anchor: { الذين } في محل النصب على الذم ، أو الرفع على «هم الذين » ، أو الجر على وصف المذكورين عاد وثمود وفرعون

NASAFI:89:11/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:11/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:11/r2.claim: They overstepped the bounds in the lands.

QURTUBI:89:11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:11/r1.claim: Those who transgressed are Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh; they rebelled and exceeded the bounds in injustice and aggression.
QURTUBI:89:11/r1.anchor: " طغوا " أي تمردوا وعتوا وتجاوزوا القدر في الظلم والعدوان
